- When sentiment is consistently negative or low (e.g., 0.00–0.33), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 20–40% for the next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 5x historical mean), model often overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to 1.5x the prior peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model often over-optimistic; apply 10–20% downward bias to avoid “sentiment inflation”.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.33–1.00), model tends to overfit short-term noise; use 7-day rolling mean to filter out erratic spikes.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 0.5x historical mean, model is underestimating long-term mean reversion; add 0.1–0.3 to forecast for next 10 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “negative sentiment → price drop” patterns, model often fails to anticipate the drop; add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment to adjust forecast downward.
